verdicts.evidence: Live homepage GET https://www.basspro.ca/home -> HTTP 200, 57352B decompressed. Grep on line 189 of the served HTML returned literal tokens: wcParamJs, 10052, 10151, prodlivengca (matched 6 times). robots.txt line 8 references /webapp/wcs/stores/servlet/sitemap_10151.xml.gz (the WebSphere-style storeId-suffixed sitemap path). These are unambiguous IBM/HCL WC fingerprints. DB's 'generic-retail' was the adapter-fallback label, not a fingerprinted platform.

curl -sI on /home returned header X-Akam-SW-Version: 0.5.0 and Set-Cookie: akavpau_c_=1779679932~... (Domain=www.basspro.ca; Path=/; HttpOnly; Secure; SameSite=None). Page-2 probe /l/firearms?page=2&firstResult=12 returned 200/2060B Akamai behavioral challenge body with literal 'Powered and protected by Akamai' + img src https://www.akamai.com/site/ko/images/logo/akamai-logo1.svg + service-worker script akam-sw.js v1.3.6. No Imperva markers (incap_ses / visid_incap cookies, X-Iinfo header) seen. DB's '-or-imperva' hedge is unsupported.

Fetched /webapp/wcs/stores/servlet/sitemap_10151.xml.gz -> 200, 289311B gzip, decompresses to 2.22MB XML. Grep '<loc>https?://[^<]*?/p/[a-z0-9-]+' = 16526 matches (R1 reported 16543, 17-item drift consistent with normal catalog turnover over ~2 days). DB's null reflected investigator never opened the .gz sitemap path listed in robots.txt line 8.

product-count-probe.ts:110 VALID_METHOD_NAMES includes both 'generic-product-sitemap' (line 117) and 'stream-page-count' (line 121). Live sitemap GET succeeded (above) so generic-product-sitemap is achievable; stream-page-count requires walking /l/ paginated pages which Akamai blocks at page 2 (verified above).

DB path test: GET /search?q=glock -> HTTP 404 (49556B SPA shell). R1 path test: GET .../SearchDisplay?storeId=10151&catalogId=10052&langId=-1&searchTerm=glock -> HTTP 200, 90915B body, grep totalSearchCount returns 'totalSearchCount:12, totalCount:12' at line 17992. Same URL with searchTerm=xyz789nonsense -> HTTP 200, 49401B body, grep returns 'totalSearchCount:0, totalCount:0' at line 3067. Size delta 90915 vs 49401 + matching count delta 12 vs 0 confirms the endpoint differentiates real vs junk queries. B3 junk-keyword diff test PASSED. Note: R1 candidate uses langId=-10; I tested langId=-1 — both returned identical totalCount pattern, so this param is forgiving.

Confirmed: GET /l/firearms returned 56675B SSR HTML with ZERO matches for regex '/p/[a-z0-9-]+' — the category page renders products client-side, so a static fetcher would extract no products. needsPlaywright is correct on both sides.

Sitemap has 16526 /p/<slug> URLs and 0 /shop/ca/<slug> URLs (the /shop/ca/ form appears only inside SearchDisplay response bodies as cross-references). R1's productUrlSchemes correctly captures both surfaces.

verdicts.verdict: r1-wins-on-shape (dept-spine), but DB's leaf gaps are real and should be merged
verdicts.evidence: All 13 DB /l/* slugs exist in sitemap (lines 7074, 12846, 15471, 15474, 15477, 15492, 17613, 17616, 17619, 17625, 17817, 18591, 19986). All 3 R1 /c/* slugs exist in sitemap (lines 3012, 11871, 14823). Sitemap ALSO has 5 firearm-relevant /l/ slugs that DB is missing: /l/firearms (14826), /l/red-dot (12855), /l/optics-accessories (12864), /l/primers-powder (18573), /l/magazines (19890). Live walk to prove minimum-cover is impossible (Akamai blocked even single-page burst on /l/firearms 403 at burst position 5/8). R1's 3-/c/ dept-spine is structurally correct per SKILL.md topLevelCategories rule but does not address that the original DB approach was leaf-focused. Recommend R4 merges: keep R1's 3 /c/* as catalogUrls (SKILL.md compliance) AND store the 18 firearm-relevant /l/* leaves in topLevelCategories.categories as the operational walk targets.

All my single-GET probes that succeeded used the R1-recommended UA. Note: I did not perform a head-to-head test of Safari vs Chrome on the same fresh session (would cost a probe budget and Akamai might re-403 the 2nd UA). R1's perUaStatusTimeline evidence stands; not contradicted by my probe path.

DB's 'none-known' and R1's null both convey 'no working bypass yet.' Neither claims a method. R1 may have intended wafWorkaround.method='none-known' but emitted null at top level; this is a schema-shape diff that R4 should normalize.

/l/firearms?page=2&firstResult=12 returned the Akamai behavioral challenge interstitial (200/2060B with sec-if-cpt-container + akam-sw.js v1.3.6). Could not enumerate page-1 product count nor page-2 product count to confirm perPage. Robots.txt line 33 'Allow: /l/*?page=*&firstResult=*' is the only signal — the firstResult value used in the canonical URL pattern would be the perPage. R1's inference of 12 derives from this; DB's 20 has no live source. Both unverified.
Same Akamai block on page-2 probe prevents verification. Pattern shape is plausible from robots.txt allow rule; perPage:12 inherits the same uncertainty as field above.

3-outcome counter-control test requires fetching the same /l/ page with two sort params and a known-bad param, then comparing first-product slugs. Akamai blocks the necessary page-2 fetches. R1's null is honest; DB's null lacks the 'sortVerified:false' annotation but is otherwise compatible.

DB pre-dates the watermark/maintain split. R1's full-catalog-sweep is operationally correct given (a) no exposed product-list API, (b) Akamai blocks pagination so navigate-from-watermark is infeasible, (c) sitemap can be walked once via .gz fetch. Reason text in R1 is accurate. R4 should adopt the new shape.
Both agree. Per-product detail-page polling is the only verify path given no exposed JSON. Operationally expensive but correctly identified by both.
